title: Links, Privacy And Launch Prep
userRequest:
## Summary

The GitHub repo moved from `nseldeib/harvardintech` to `codeyam-ai/harvardintech`, so the team's preview link now returns 404. The preview's real address is https://codeyam-ai.github.io/harvardintech/. This plan does four things:

1. **Fixes the addresses.** Every doc and review link moves to the new preview address. The content editor is pointed at the new GitHub account, `codeyam-ai`.
2. **Makes search and share links name harvardintech.com.** The preview stays hidden from search engines. Share cards, canonical links and structured data name harvardintech.com, never the preview address.
3. **Keeps internal material off the public site.** That covers the 170 component test pages (which carry made-up bios under real board members' names), the redesign gallery and the placeholder video folder. The status page and the donor deck default to staying off the public site until Ben and Nicole decide.
4. **Takes the preview password out of the repo and docs, and writes the launch-day checklist.**

Nothing here makes anything public. harvardintech.com stays on Strikingly until the owner is ready.

## Owner decisions (2026-09-14)

- **Dead preview link.** "Fix the link." Update every doc and review link to the new address.
- **Content editor account.** Plan it: "Make sure we fix this."
- **Search and share links (PAGES_SITE).** Plan it: "we should not have this indexed at all; it should all be for the live harvardintech.com site."
- **Preview password is effectively public.** Plan it: "Discuss how best to fix this."
- **~170 internal test pages.** Undecided: "I'd like to understand what these are? Is this related to the CMS?"
- **Status page and donor-wall deck.** Undecided: "This needs to be discussed with Ben and Nicole."
- **20 MB redesign gallery.** Plan it: "Include a review of that content."
- **Placeholder video folder.** Plan it.
- **Launch-day settings.** "Yes, we'll want a launch checklist."

### What the ~170 test pages are (plain answer)

They are **not the CMS.** They are screenshot pages for the project tooling (codeyam). Each one renders a single component, such as a board tile, a donor card or a deploy banner, in one fixed state, so the tool can photograph it. There are 81 standalone pages plus 89 generated by one route file, `src/pages/isolated-components/[name].astro`: 170 in total. The tool only ever needs them on the local dev server. Today they ship with every deployed build, and they are not behind the passphrase.

Some of them show sample bios under real board names (Ben Wei, Peter Boyce, Krysia Lenzo, Jessica Li, Nadia Eldeib). These come from `BOARD_BIOS` in `[name].astro`, `BoardMemberTile.astro` and `BoardMemberTile-Initials.astro`. On a public build, all 170 pages would also land in `sitemap.xml`.

## Open questions / needs input

1. **For Ben and Nicole: the status page (`public/review/index.html`) and the donor-wall deck (`public/donor-network.html`).** Options:
   - (a) Keep them on the private preview only. This is the default this plan builds; the public build leaves them out.
   - (b) Retire them. Move the useful parts into the cutover runbook or a shared doc, then delete both files.
   - (c) Publish them on purpose. Not recommended. The status page is internal project notes, and the deck holds sample supporter names.

   Nicole should also confirm the deck's supporter names are invented (for example "Margaret Chen-Alvarez" and "Robert K. Whitmore").
2. **For the owner: the redesign gallery.** Can it be archived now that a direction is built? See the content review in step 6.
3. **For Jared: the parked plan.** Does `.codeyam/plans/one-site-content-edits-publish-straight-to-main.md` run before or after this one? Both edit `src/data/cms.json` and `docs/nicole-review.md`. This plan changes only `repo.owner`, `siteUrl` and the links. The parked plan owns `branch`, the staging track and the one-site rewrite. Whichever runs second rebases onto the first. The parked plan's own links say `nseldeib.github.io/harvardintech`, and they must become the new address.
4. **For Ben: harvardintech.com's registrar.** Ben holds the domain at GoDaddy. Launch day needs him to make the DNS change (checklist item 7).

## Recommendations

### A. Search and share links (PAGES_SITE)
- **Option 1:** set `PAGES_SITE` to `https://codeyam-ai.github.io`. This fixes the dead address, but share cards would still advertise the preview.
- **Option 2:** set `PAGES_SITE` to `https://harvardintech.com` today. This breaks the links, because `/harvardintech` stays in every canonical URL.
- **Option 3 (pick):** add a separate `CANONICAL_ORIGIN` setting, `https://harvardintech.com`. Canonical links, share cards, structured data, `llms.txt` and the sitemap line in robots.txt are built from it, with the base path removed. `PAGES_SITE` becomes `https://codeyam-ai.github.io`, because that is where the preview really is.

  Why: this matches the owner's note exactly. Every advertised URL names the live site, and the preview stays `noindex` plus `Disallow: /`. At launch the two values meet, and `CANONICAL_ORIGIN` can fall back to `site`.

### B. The preview password
The password is effectively public. It sits in plain text in `src/lib/previewGate.ts` (as the default), `public/review/index.html:473`, `public/donor-network.html:1892`, `docs/nicole-review.md` and `DEPLOY_SETUP.md:189`. It is also in git history, so it has to be changed, not just hidden.

- **Option 1 (pick):** change the password and keep it only in a secret. Store it as a GitHub Actions secret, `PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE`. Remove the default from the code, so a gated build without the secret fails. Commit a placeholder in the two static files and fill it in at build time. Remove it from every doc, and share it only through a password manager.

  Why: cheap, and it closes every place the password leaks from the repo. It is still a deterrent, not real protection: anyone who can load the page can read the check in its source. That is proportionate for content that goes public at launch anyway.
- **Option 2:** real server-side access control, such as Cloudflare Access or a password-protected Netlify or Cloudflare Pages host in front of the preview. This is genuinely private but means new hosting and accounts. Worth it for the launch-day private editor site if the team wants real locks. That can be decided then.
- **Option 3:** encrypt each page's content with the password (the approach the editor already uses for password-protected previews). Strong, but it breaks assets and search across a whole site. Overkill here.

### C. Keeping internal files off the public site
- **Option 1:** hand-migrate the test pages elsewhere. Rejected. The tooling's isolation-route migration has no Astro path.
- **Option 2:** a `getStaticPaths` guard plus a sitemap filter. This only reaches the 89 generated pages. The 81 standalone pages and the raw `public/` files have no `getStaticPaths`.
- **Option 3 (pick):** a small build step removes a named list of internal paths from `dist/` on the public build, plus a sitemap filter for the same list, plus the `getStaticPaths` guard in `[name].astro`.

  Why: one list in `src/lib/publishTrack.ts` covers the test pages and the `public/` files alike, and it is unit-testable. It follows the pattern the cutover runbook already uses (`includeCutoverRunbook`). The tooling keeps working, because it captures against `astro dev`.

## Implementation

1. **Local remote (a one-time command, no file change).** Run `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/codeyam-ai/harvardintech`. Then update the clone URL in `README.md:101`.
2. **Point the content editor at the new account.**
   - `src/data/cms.json`: set `repo.owner` to `codeyam-ai` and `siteUrl` to the new preview address. Leave `branch` alone; the parked plan owns it.
   - `src/data/settings.json`: set `siteUrl` to match.
   - `CMS_SETUP.md:214, 348, 352, 356`: change `nseldeib/harvardintech` to `codeyam-ai/harvardintech`, and remind readers that fine-grained tokens must be re-created under the new owner.
   - The runbook reads `cmsConfig.repo` (`src/pages/cutover-runbook/[...path].astro:58`), so it follows automatically.
3. **Search and share links.**
   - `src/lib/canonicalUrl.ts` (new): add `canonicalFor(pathname, base, origin)`. It removes `base` from the path and joins the rest onto `origin`.
   - `astro.config.mjs`: at line 411, change the fallback from `https://nseldeib.github.io` to `https://harvardintech.com`, and expose `CANONICAL_ORIGIN` to the pages. Rewrite the header comments at lines 413–418 for the new owner.
   - Use `canonicalFor` in `src/components/SEO.astro` (line 32, which sets the canonical and `og:url`), `src/components/StructuredData.astro` (line 14), `src/pages/llms.txt.ts` (line 13) and `src/pages/robots.txt.ts` (the `Sitemap:` URL).
   - `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `build` job: set `PAGES_SITE: https://codeyam-ai.github.io` and add `CANONICAL_ORIGIN: https://harvardintech.com`.
   - Do not touch the `review` job or the staging push target (lines 196–237). They stay under the old owner and belong to the parked plan.
4. **Update every doc and review link to https://codeyam-ai.github.io/harvardintech/.**
   - `docs/nicole-review.md`: lines 15–19, 61–65 and 248.
   - `DEPLOY_SETUP.md`: line 12.
   - `docs/scoping/README.md`: lines 58 and 124.
   - `docs/scoping/domain-transfer-runbook.md`: lines 87 and 97.
   - `CMS_SETUP.md`: lines 356 and 401.
   - The link text in `public/review/index.html`.
   - Staging links (`-staging`) stay as they are, because the staging site is still under the old owner.
5. **Internal-path exclusion (Recommendation C).**
   - `src/lib/publishTrack.ts`: add `INTERNAL_PATHS`. Its entries are `isolated-components`, `design-review-4ece6c14`, `videos/README.md`, `review` and `donor-network.html`; the last two are the Ben and Nicole default. Add `excludedFromBuild(isDev, isReviewTrack)`:
     - dev: nothing is excluded;
     - review track: `isolated-components` and `videos/README.md` are excluded;
     - public track: everything in `INTERNAL_PATHS` is excluded.

     Also add `isInternalPath(url)`.
   - `src/pages/isolated-components/[name].astro`, `getStaticPaths` at line 817: return `[]` unless `import.meta.env.DEV`. This copies the guard in `src/pages/cutover-runbook/[...path].astro:47–54`.
   - `astro.config.mjs`: add an `astro:build:done` integration that deletes each excluded path from `dist/`. Extend the sitemap filter at line 447 to `!isPreviewUrl(page) && !isInternalPath(page)`.
   - `src/lib/sitePages.ts`: add `videos` and `donor-network.html` to `RESERVED_PAGE_SLUGS`. Keep the existing entries; they are still served on dev and preview.
6. **Redesign gallery: content review, then exclude it.** Inventory of `public/design-review-4ece6c14/`:
   - 14 files, 20 MB: 13 mockups plus `index.html`, each 1.9–2.8 MB.
   - 139 images embedded inside the pages themselves (67 JPEG, 72 PNG).
   - The five real board members' names appear 13 times each, and `ben@harvardintech.com` appears 12 times.
   - Every file carries `noindex`, but none is passphrase-gated. The unguessable URL is the only protection.
   - One direction is titled "Letters to Sean".

   Steps:
   - (a) Walk the 13 mockups with the owner. Record whether any image is a real person's photo, and whether any copy is an invented quote attributed to a real person.
   - (b) Exclude the gallery from the public build (step 5).
   - (c) If the owner confirms the direction is settled (Open question 2), move the folder to `.codeyam/design/` and drop it from `RESERVED_PAGE_SLUGS`. Update the references in `src/lib/previewGate.ts` (the comment), `docs/nicole-review.md:43` and `src/components/cutover/OperatorDetail.astro`.
7. **Placeholder video folder.**
   - `public/videos/README.md`: move it to `docs/hero-videos.md` (new), so the internal notes stop being served.
   - Keep `public/videos/sample-backdrop.mp4`. The scenario `src/pages/isolated-components/MomentumHero-Video.astro` uses it, and it is 10 KB of flat crimson.
   - Add a comment in `src/lib/publishTrack.ts` saying the folder is replaced when real footage arrives.
8. **Preview password (Recommendation B, Option 1).**
   - `src/lib/previewGate.ts`: remove the `'crimson2026'` default. Add `assertPassphraseConfigured()`, which throws when the gate is on and the secret is empty. Call it from `src/components/PreviewGate.astro`.
   - `public/review/index.html:473` and `public/donor-network.html:1892`: replace the literal with `__PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE__`.
   - The `astro:build:done` integration from step 5 replaces the placeholder in `dist/` with the secret.
   - `.codeyam/design/donor-network/build.py`: stop parsing the default; emit the placeholder instead. `src/lib/reviewGate.js` already refuses an empty password.
   - `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `build` job: add `PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE }}`.
   - Remove the password from `docs/nicole-review.md` (lines 15–20 and 59) and `DEPLOY_SETUP.md:189–190`. Replace it with "shared privately; see the password manager".
   - Owner action: create the secret with a new password in the `codeyam-ai/harvardintech` repo settings, and send it to reviewers out of band.
9. **Launch checklist.** Add `## Launch day checklist` to `DEPLOY_SETUP.md`, replacing the scattered notes under "At the cutover: the roles swap". It contains the text below, and the runbook links to it.

   **Launch day checklist**

   1. Set `PAGES_SITE` to `https://harvardintech.com` in the `build` job of `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. `CANONICAL_ORIGIN` then matches it and can be deleted.
   2. Drop `DEPLOY_BASE_PATH` from the `build` job, so the base is `/`.
   3. Remove `PREVIEW_GATE` and `INCLUDE_DRAFTS` from the public build. Do this only in the same change that stands up the private editor site (item 5). In the same change, flip `gates both tracks while neither is meant to be public` in `src/lib/deployTracks.test.ts`.
   4. Add the custom domain under Settings → Pages in `codeyam-ai/harvardintech`, wait for the certificate, then tick **Enforce HTTPS**.
   5. Stand up the private editor site: a gated build of `main` with `/admin`, at review.harvardintech.com, as described in the parked plan (`.codeyam/plans/one-site-content-edits-publish-straight-to-main.md`).
   6. Create a new `PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE` secret for the private editor site, different from the preview's, and share it only through the password manager.
   7. DNS: the GoDaddy account owner is Ben. He changes the apex and `www` records from Strikingly to GitHub Pages and adds the `review` record.
   8. Redirects from old Strikingly URLs: the redirects themselves live in another plan. Confirm that plan has shipped before the DNS change.
   9. After deploy, verify:
      - `robots.txt` says `Allow: /` and points at `https://harvardintech.com/sitemap-index.xml`;
      - the sitemap contains no `/isolated-components`, `/review`, `/design-review-*` or `/donor-network.html` URLs, and each of those paths returns 404;
      - `/admin` returns 404;
      - a page's canonical link and `og:url` start with `https://harvardintech.com/`.

## Tests

- `src/lib/canonicalUrl.test.ts` (new): `canonicalFor` removes the `/harvardintech` base, keeps a root base unchanged, never doubles slashes, and always returns a URL on the given origin.
- `src/lib/publishTrack.test.ts`: `excludedFromBuild` returns nothing in dev. On the review track it returns `isolated-components` and `videos/README.md`. On the public track it returns every entry in `INTERNAL_PATHS`. `isInternalPath` matches `/harvardintech/isolated-components/BoardMemberTile/` and `/design-review-4ece6c14/index.html`, but not `/blog/` or `/volunteer/`.
- `src/lib/previewGate.test.ts`: without a secret, `PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE` is empty and never `'crimson2026'`. `assertPassphraseConfigured` throws when the gate is on and the secret is unset.
- `src/lib/deployTracks.test.ts`, new cases in the `build` job:
  - `PAGES_SITE` is `https://codeyam-ai.github.io`;
  - `CANONICAL_ORIGIN` is `https://harvardintech.com`;
  - `PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE` comes from `secrets.`.

  The existing gating assertion stays.
- `src/lib/docLinks.test.ts` (new): it reads `docs/nicole-review.md`, `DEPLOY_SETUP.md`, `CMS_SETUP.md`, `docs/scoping/*.md`, `README.md` and `src/data/cms.json`. It asserts that none contains `nseldeib.github.io/harvardintech/` (the dead reviewed link; the `-staging` host is allowed), and that none of those docs, `public/review/index.html` or `public/donor-network.html` contains `crimson2026`. It also asserts that `cms.json`'s `repo.owner` is `codeyam-ai`.
- `src/lib/seoEndpoints.test.ts`: the robots `Sitemap:` line and the `llms.txt` absolute URLs use the canonical origin, with no base path.
- `src/lib/sitePages.test.ts`: the existing "covers every hand-built top-level route" and "holds no duplicates" cases pass with `videos` and `donor-network.html` added.
- `src/lib/deployWatch.test.ts`: fix the comment at line 16 so it names the new reviewed address.

## Scenarios to Demonstrate

- The home page's page source: canonical and `og:url` are `https://harvardintech.com/`. This is a production-build check (`astro build` and serve), because dev leaves the base at `/`.
- The existing `BoardMemberTile` and `MomentumHero-Video` isolation scenarios still capture under `astro dev`. This shows the harness is untouched for the tooling.
- The cutover runbook scenarios (`.codeyam/scenarios/cutover-runbook-*.json`): the records panel names `codeyam-ai/harvardintech`.
- The `donor-network.html` and `review/` gates on a gated build: the new password opens them and `crimson2026` does not. This is a build-time check, not a dev scenario.

## Out of scope

- The staging track, the editor's `branch`, `promote.yml` and the one-site rewrite: the parked plan owns these.
- Creating the redirects themselves (another plan).
- The DNS cutover itself, and any change to Strikingly or GoDaddy.
- Real server-side access control (Recommendation B, Option 2). This is a launch-time decision for the private editor site.
- Hand-migrating the isolation pages, or changing how the tooling captures them.
- Rewriting the old owner's staging repository (`nseldeib/harvardintech-staging`) or its deploy key.
- The final fate of the status page and donor deck (Open question 1). This plan only keeps them off the public build.
description: Fixed every team link and the content editor for the repo move to codeyam-ai, and made canonical links, share cards, structured data, llms.txt and the robots.txt sitemap line name harvardintech.com through a new CANONICAL_ORIGIN setting. Internal material now stays off the public build — the component screenshot pages, the redesign gallery, the status page and the donor deck — and the preview passphrase moved out of the repo into the PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE secret, with a gated build that fails loudly without it. Also corrected the cutover runbook DNS target to codeyam-ai.github.io, added a launch-day checklist to DEPLOY_SETUP.md, and queued a follow-up plan built from Nicole review video of 2026-09-14. Scope verdict: no open project deliverables, so none delivered or deferred this cycle. Owner action before the next deploy: create the PREVIEW_GATE_PASSPHRASE secret. Deviation from the plan: the editor site address stays on the staging site, because the editor still commits to the staging branch.
